Hon'ble Dr. Gautam Chowdhary,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

This application has been filed for quashing of the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 815 of 2021 Lotai Vs. Hari Kishan Agrahari and another) and order dated 04.05.2022 summoning the applicants under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C., Police Station Chunar, District Mirzapur,
pending in the court of First Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Mirzapur.

entities.text: Complaint Case No. 815 of 2021 Lotai Vs. Hari Kishan Agrahari and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: First Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Mirzapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
On perusal of the record, the Court finds that the allegations made in the complaint disclose commission of a cognizable offence and those allegations have found support in the statements Harikishan Agrahari And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79208467/
1 recorded under Sections 200 and 202 Cr.P.C. on the basis whereof the summoning order has been passed against the applicants.

entities.text: Harikishan Agrahari And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court in exercise of its power under section 482 Cr.P.C., is not required to assess the correctness of the allegation and the reliability of the evidence, the prayer to quash the summoning order and the consequential proceeding is rejected.

At this stage, the learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants have so far not been arrested in the above case and the police is seeking to arrest the applicants and there may be coercive processes issued against the applicants by the court concerned therefore, some direction may be issued to the court concerned for consideration of the bail prayer of the applicants.
As the Apex Court in Satendra Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No. 5191 of 2021, decided on 07.10.2021) has already laid down guidelines for grant of bail, without fettering the discretion of the courts concerned and the statutory provisions governing consideration in grant of bail, no specific direction need be issued by this Court as it is expected that the court concerned will take into consideration the necessary guidelines already issued by the Apex court.
With the aforesaid observations, the application is disposed off.
Order Date :- 14.6.2024 Rmk.
 
Harikishan Agrahari
